chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you Name (Bismillah) during the Ablution (Wudu), your entire body becomes pure, and when you do not Name, nothing from your body becomes pure except what the water passes over.
ai.seo_question: Does reciting Bismillah affect the validity of ritual purity in Wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic debate on whether 'Bismillah' is a mandatory condition (shart) for the validity of Wudu or merely a recommended act (mustahabb) that affects the completeness of purification. Shia scholars, particularly in the Usuli school, often interpret this to mean that while the ritual remains valid without it, the spiritual perfection and full efficacy of the purification are contingent upon invoking God's name, reflecting the principle that ritual acts require both physical execution and spiritual intention.
